## Abstract

Student persistence remains an important question for institutions of
higher education. In this study, we use logistic regression to investigate
the relationship between measures of academic preparation, first-semester
performance, and first-year persistence.

Using an anonymized dataset of 2,418 students, we compare candidate models
using cross-validation and evaluate predictive performance using ROC AUC,
sensitivity, and specificity. First-semester GPA and credit completion
emerge as the strongest predictors of persistence.

The results illustrate both the usefulness and limitations of predictive
models in educational settings and emphasize the importance of considering
ethical implications when using student-level data.

**Keywords:** logistic regression, education, cross-validation, predictive modeling
